title: Sri Lanka uses air force drones to tackle spreading dengue outbreak - Reuters
snippet: ## Browse World. ## Browse Business. Image 3: A white board with general information on dengue patients inside a ward at District General Hospital in Negombo. Item 1 of 9 A white board with general information on dengue patients inside a ward at District General Hospital in Negombo, Sri Lanka, July 16, 2026. **[1/9]**A white board with general information on dengue patients inside a ward at District General Hospital in Negombo, Sri Lanka, July 16, 2026. COLOMBO, July 21 (Reuters) - Sri Lanka's public health services and hospitals are battling the worst outbreak of mosquito-borne dengue in nearly a decade, and turning ​to the island nation's armed forces to help curb the spread of the disease. Hospitals rushed ​to add beds, convert wards to care for the ill and step up hours worked by doctors and nurses in the battle to treat an influx of more ​than 18,000 cases in the first two weeks of July, health authorities said.
